title: React SSR Core Check
description: Check your understanding of CSR, SSR, SSG, React Server Components, Next.js, hydration, mismatches, streaming, and rendering strategy tradeoffs.
author: DailyCoder

questions.prompt: What does client-side rendering primarily mean?

options.text: The browser downloads JavaScript and React builds much of the UI on the client
Every page is generated only at build time

questions.explanation: In CSR, the browser runs JavaScript to render the app UI, often after receiving a minimal HTML shell.

questions.prompt: What does server-side rendering produce for an initial request?

options.text: HTML generated on the server for that request

questions.explanation: SSR renders HTML on the server, which can improve first content and SEO for suitable pages.

questions.prompt: What is static site generation best suited for?

options.text: Pages that can be generated ahead of time and do not need per-request personalization
Highly personalized dashboards requiring fresh data on every request

questions.explanation: SSG creates pages at build time or regeneration time, making it a good fit for content that is mostly stable.

options.text: React attaching event handlers and state to server-rendered HTML in the browser
A CSS media query for dark mode

questions.explanation: Hydration bridges server HTML and the interactive client React tree.

questions.prompt: Server Components and SSR are the same thing.
questions.explanation: React Server Components define where components execute and what is sent to the client. SSR is a rendering strategy for producing HTML.

questions.prompt: Which values can commonly cause hydration mismatches if rendered differently on server and client? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Browser-only state such as `window.innerWidth` during initial render
A stable prop passed from the server

questions.explanation: Initial server and client output must match. Time, randomness, and browser-only values often differ.

questions.prompt: In the Next.js App Router, what is an important mental model?

options.text: Components are Server Components by default unless marked with `use client`
All components are browser-only by default
There is no server rendering support

questions.explanation: The App Router defaults to Server Components, with client boundaries declared explicitly.

questions.prompt: What can streaming with Suspense improve?

options.text: It can send parts of the UI as they become ready instead of waiting for everything
It makes every component a client component

questions.explanation: Streaming lets the server progressively send HTML for ready boundaries, improving perceived loading for suitable pages.
